title: Maximum 20-Layer DBR-Backed Chromium Absorber
scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 17 to 20 provides additional interference degrees of freedom that can sharpen the visible-NIR transition boundary, improving the weighted spectral selectivity score beyond 0.5159.
design_principle: Use all 20 allowed layers with Cr at the Al interface followed by 19 dielectric layers (HfO2/SiO2 alternating). Initialize thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness at 550 nm (visible center) for dielectrics and 15 nm for Cr absorption layer.
proposed_topology: Air | Cr(15nm) | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Al substrate. Total 20 finite layers (1 Cr + 19 dielectric).
manufacturing_considerations: Cr layer thickness critical for absorption vs. IR reflectance trade-off
theory_basis: Admittance Locus Method for metal-dielectric multilayer optimization
DMD interference design principle for spectral separation
expected_advantages: More layers enable sharper spectral transition
Better control over visible-band anti-reflection condition
Potential to exceed 0.5159 score ceiling from 17L runs
known_risks: Optimizer may struggle with higher-dimensional search space
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer stack on Al substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 (20 finite layers total). Initialize Cr at 15 nm, all dielectrics at quarter-wave optical thickness referenced to 550 nm. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses in bounds [10, 300] nm using gradient_thickness optimizer with Adam-LBFGS hybrid. Wavelength bands: 400-700 nm (maximize absorptance), 700-2000 nm (maximize reflectance). Normal unpolarized incidence. Total layer count constraint: exactly 20 layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Changed layer count from 17 to 20 to test if maximum allowed complexity improves spectral selectivity score beyond prior 0.5159 ceiling.
